conventions.convention: The reference simplex is open; mesh cells are closed nondegenerate simplices. The domain is the interior of their union, and intersections are whole faces. Mesh dimension is d≥2.
Reference maps have det A>0. Shape regularity bounds diameter divided by inradius, where inradius means radius rather than diameter of the inscribed ball.
C₋₁=0 and ∂₀=0; higher boundaries use the alternating vertex-deletion formula, with permutation signs identifying oriented faces.
Conformity means equality of polynomial traces on interior facets. Zero boundary conditions mean zero polynomial traces on boundary facets; Sobolev membership is a separate theorem.

Unisolvence is bijectivity of the degree-of-freedom map. Interpolation on a larger normed space requires well-defined bounded extensions of those functionals. The zero-dimensional element and empty interpolation sum are permitted.
Smooth Sobolev norm density is asserted only for finite p. Simplex face traces and their Green identity are stated for real functions with 1<p<∞.
The contravariant pushforward is A v̂/det A; the covariant pushforward is A⁻ᵀv̂. Curl is scalar in dimension two and vector-valued in dimension three, with bilinear weak test pairings.
Automatic finite-p nodal boundedness requires integer ℓ>d/p and the Axiom of Choice; p=∞ permits every integer ℓ≥1. The only critical unboundedness case established here is two-dimensional H¹.

load_bearing.statement: Assuming Countable Choice, an invertible affine bijection between bounded open sets preserves W^{r,p} under pullback for every integer r≥0 and 1≤p≤∞. Weak derivatives obey the constant-matrix chain rule, and order-m seminorms have the stated matrix-power and absolute-determinant factors, with corresponding reverse estimates.

Assuming Countable Choice, a C¹ vector field on a nondegenerate affine simplex satisfies the outward-facet Gauss–Green formula. Under an orientation-preserving affine map, the oriented area element is det(A)A⁻ᵀn̂ dŜ.

Assuming Countable Choice, on a bounded polyhedral open set with a finite matching affine simplicial mesh, every real conforming piecewise polynomial with zero boundary-facet traces belongs to W₀^{1,p} for 1≤p<∞ and satisfies a Poincare inequality.

Assuming Countable Choice, for finite p, integer r≥1, integer s≥0 and real v∈W^{max(r,s),p}, the polynomial q∈P_{r−1} matching all derivative means through order r−1 satisfies the stated W^{s,p} bound by the order-r seminorm when s≤r, and by the sum of seminorms of orders r through s when s>r.

Assuming Countable Choice, a fixed unisolvent polynomial reference element containing P_k with degrees of freedom bounded on W^{ℓ,p}, 1≤p<∞, has uniform affine-mesh error bounds h_K^{r−m}|v|_{W^{r,p}} when ℓ≤r≤k+1 and 0≤m≤r. When ℓ>k+1 and 0≤m≤k+1, the bound is the sum of h_K^{n−m}|v|_{W^{n,p}} for k+1≤n≤ℓ.
Assuming the Axiom of Choice, for d≥2, every integer k≥0 and 1≤p≤∞, the reference simplex has a bounded linear W^{k,p} extension to R^d, with support in one fixed bounded set.
Assuming Countable Choice, for every 1≤p<∞, the L^p norm of a real W^{1,p} function minus its reference-simplex mean is bounded by a constant times its first-order Sobolev seminorm.

Assuming Countable Choice, in dimensions two and three, positive-determinant affine Piola maps preserve the stated H(div) and H(curl) graph spaces and obey the stated weak differential identities. The scalar gradient identity holds for W^{1,2}; normal-flux and tangential moment formulas are asserted for smooth fields.

concerns.concern: The Statement writes “the reference triangle Ŝ₂=conv{(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)}”. The mesh definition reserves Ŝ₂ for the open simplex and its closure for this convex hull. The vertex and area computations are correct, but the example should distinguish the closed reference triangle from the open-simplex symbol.

seams_checked.note: This is background interpolation context. The assigned items prove unisolvent interpolation locally and do not import a univariate cardinal-node theorem as multivariate unisolvence.

The spatial-rate corollary retains bounded unisolvent reference degrees of freedom, polynomial reproduction, ℓ≤r≤k+1, shape regularity, and an explicitly assumed globally conforming boundary-preserving interpolant.

Cell-average projection uses the matching mesh convention. Its H¹ error proof uses reference Poincare–Wirtinger and affine pullback with cancelling determinant factors; only an upper bound on the affine matrix is needed, so the absence of shape regularity there is sound.

The primal approximation corollary uses unisolvence, bounded W^{r+1,2} degrees of freedom, Bramble–Hilbert and shape-regular scaling faithfully. Global conformity and zero-boundary preservation remain explicit assumptions.
The Ritz definition assumes conformity. The concrete semidiscrete theorem and fan-mesh examples use the real p=2 zero-boundary polynomial inclusion with Countable Choice retained.

The abstract A-page results assume conforming trial spaces. The square example obtains H₀¹ membership from matching zero-boundary polynomials; the broken degree-zero example explicitly fails conformity and does not invoke the conforming upper bound.

The affine P1 corollary assumes bounded reference nodal functionals on W^{2,2} and global conformity. It applies the generic local estimate with ℓ=r=2 and m=1, without deriving automatic nodal boundedness under only Countable Choice.
